title: Microsoft Purview DLP: actionable email notifications for OneDrive and SharePoint files
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, notification actions, licensing baseline and audit controls are supported. Minor corrections should restore omitted wizard headings in the notification path and assess risk before an administrator enables the actions.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: Users can initiate remediation of OneDrive and SharePoint policy matches directly from notification emails.
claims.quote: These controls enable users to fix the issue that caused the DLP policy match or otherwise remediate issues on OneDrive folders or SharePoint sites directly from the email.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn still marks actionable email notifications for OneDrive and SharePoint as preview.
claims.quote: Actionable email notifications for OneDrive and SharePoint workloads are in preview.

claims.claim: Custom end-user notification templates are configured per DLP rule.
claims.quote: You can create a custom email notification template for end user email notifications for each rule. Then send it instead of sending the default email notification.

claims.claim: The existing custom email notification option is available for policies scoped to Exchange, SharePoint and OneDrive locations.
claims.quote: This option is available for policies scoped to the Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive locations.

claims.claim: A rule's notification recipients can include the content owner.
claims.quote: For each rule in a DLP policy, you can: Send the notification to the people you choose. These people can include the owner of the content

claims.claim: A rule's notification recipients can include the person who last modified the content.
claims.quote: These people can include the owner of the content, the person who last modified the content, the owner of the site where the content is stored, or a specific user.

claims.claim: A rule's notification recipients can include the owner of the site containing the content.
claims.quote: These people can include the owner of the content, the person who last modified the content, the owner of the site where the content is stored, or a specific user.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A rule's notification recipients can include a specific user.
claims.quote: These people can include the owner of the content, the person who last modified the content, the owner of the site where the content is stored, or a specific user.

claims.claim: Email notifications go only to individual recipients, not groups or distribution lists.
claims.quote: You can send email notifications only to individual recipients, not to groups or distribution lists.

claims.claim: Only new content triggers an email notification.
claims.quote: Only new content triggers an email notification. Editing existing content triggers policy tips, but not email notifications.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Notification emails are sent unprotected.
claims.quote: Notification emails are sent unprotected.

claims.claim: External senders receive a templated notification without full details to limit disclosure of policy configuration.
claims.quote: External senders receive only a templatized notification without full details to prevent any unintended loss of information about the policy configuration.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The new actions require administrator configuration, so existing notification content does not acquire them if the administrator does nothing.
claims.quote: To make these options available to your users in notification emails, select them when you configure the email notification.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview portal creation path reaches a rule's User Notifications control.
claims.quote: On the Define policy settings page, the Create or customize advanced DLP rules option should already be selected. Select Next. On the Customize advanced DLP rules page, select + Create rule. Set the User Notifications toggle to On.
claims.fix: In both copies, use 'Data loss prevention > Policies > Create policy > Enterprise applications & devices > Custom > Custom > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > User Notifications'. This restores the named wizard headings at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-spo-odb-external; omitted selections of administrative scope and policy locations are permitted scope-selection omissions.

claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule -Identity <rule> -NotifyEmailCustomText <text> sets the specified rule's custom notification text, rather than selecting remediation actions.
claims.quote: The NotifyEmailCustomText parameter specifies the custom text in the email notification message that's sent to recipients when the conditions of the rule are met.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search reaches the audit search page.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. If the Audit solution card isn't displayed, select View all solutions and then select Audit from the Core section. On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable:

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog searches the unified audit log.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is Search-UnifiedAuditLog. That means you can use this cmdlet to search the audit log instead of using the search tool on the Audit page in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Searching the audit log requires the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role.

claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule lists a NotifyEmailOnedriveRemediationActions parameter.
claims.quote: [-NotifyEmailOnedriveRemediationActions <NotifyEmailRemediationActions>]

claims.claim: The remediation-actions parameter has a placeholder description and no documented accepted values on the cited reference.
claims.quote: Searched: "NotifyEmailOnedriveRemediationActions" values description; read Set-DlpComplianceRule parameter section and New-DlpComplianceRule search excerpt. Set shows '{{ Fill NotifyEmailOnedriveRemediationActions Description }}' and a type, but no values or behaviour.

claims.claim: The notifications Learn page describes no separate tenant-wide switch for actionable notifications.
claims.quote: Searched: "DLP" "actionable email" "tenant" enable disable; read notifications page, Set-DlpComplianceRule and DLP policy-reference search excerpts. Configuration is per notification/rule; the notifications page describes no separate tenant-wide switch.

claims.claim: The notifications Learn page does not describe action authentication or the handling of forwarded or shared notification emails.
claims.quote: Searched: "DLP" "actionable email" "authentication" forwarded; read notifications page and search excerpts. No action-authentication or forwarding mechanism is described for these DLP actions; unrelated sender-authentication and workflow pages do not establish one.

claims.claim: The notifications Learn page does not describe an approval step for the email override action.
claims.quote: Searched: "DLP" "actionable email" "approval" automated; read notifications page and search excerpts. The action requires a business justification; no approval step is described there. Exchange message-moderation and Purview workflow approvals concern other mechanisms.

claims.claim: Learn describes user-selected actions, not automatic execution of these email actions on a user's behalf.
claims.quote: Searched: "DLP" "actionable email" "approval" automated; read notifications page and DLP policy-reference search excerpts. The notification section describes controls enabling users to remediate; it describes no automated execution of those email controls.

claims.claim: Medium risk is assigned on the basis of actions users can take after an administrator enables them.
claims.quote: risk: "medium"; defaultState: "admin-opt-in"; rationale: "Medium. Once an admin adds the actions, a recipient can delete a file, stop its sharing or override the policy from the email"; Why it matters: "Nothing reaches users until an admin selects the actions".
claims.fix: Set risk to 'low' and replace its rationale with 'Low. Actionable notifications reach users only after an administrator selects the actions in the email configuration; leaving this new option unconfigured adds no remediation actions.' The assessment scale rates the change before administrator action and explicitly places admin-opt-in changes in low risk.
